Now, one who wishes to universally make offerings and provide universal relief should prepare the ritual site with utmost sincerity and solemnity.
Having prepared incense, flowers, food, drink, pure water, and so forth according to one’s means, and having completed the arrangement of seats according to their respective positions:
Taking refuge in the Guru and the Three Jewels and generating the bodhicitta: I take refuge in the Guru. I take refuge in the Buddha. I take refuge in the Dharma. I take refuge in the Saṅgha.
I now generate the mind of enlightenment.
One does not seek for oneself the blessings and rewards of the human or celestial realms,
nor those of the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, or even the various stages of Bodhisattvas of the provisional vehicles;
rather, one relies solely on the Supreme Vehicle to give rise to the bodhicitta.
Having made the threefold aspiration,
"May all sentient beings of the dharma realm simultaneously attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi," he used the ring finger of his right hand.
Take scented water and smear it upon the palms of both hands as a sign of reverence;
since there is no altar, perform this abbreviated rite as detailed below.
Alternatively, one may add the mantras from within the Amoghapāśa Sūtra.
When smearing pure water upon the palms,
recite the mantra for purifying the hands as follows:
Oṃ āḥ muḥ kha ca la mi ma yaṃ sru sru svāhā. Recite the mantra of the Great Wheel Vidyārāja seven times silently.
Regarding the mantra-seal (mudrā):
the *Amṛtakuṇḍalī-bodhisattva-japa-vidhi* states that one interlaces the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Straighten the two index fingers so they are parallel.
Wrap the two middle fingers around the first joints of the two index fingers,
with their tips touching each other.
Extend both thumbs straight and join the mudrā at the heart;
recite the mantra: *namaḥ siddhye svāhā kha*.

one shall immediately enter all maṇḍalas,
and whatever is performed will be accomplished.
The *Dhāraṇī-vidhi* of Akṣobhya Tathāgata states:
"Place the mudrā at the heart and recite [the mantra] seven times;
continue to recite this mantra."
Just as when re-entering the maṇḍala circle,
if one loses mindfulness and breaks samādhi,
so it is for both bodhisattvas and śrāvakas.
The two types of restraint— of body and speech—
the four grave offenses, and the five acts of immediate retribution:
these and other such karmic obstacles.
All shall attain complete purity.

All of you who have resolved upon the vast mind should immediately purify your bodies and minds;
with sincere devotion and earnest prayer, take refuge in the Triple Gem:
Namo Buddha, Namo Dharma, Namo Sangha.
I now resolve upon the vast mind;
it is not for the sake of seeking the blessings and rewards of humans or devas for myself,
nor for the stages of pratyekabuddhas, śrāvakas, or even the various levels of bodhisattvas of the provisional vehicles.
Relying solely upon the Supreme Vehicle, I resolve to awaken the bodhicitta,
vowing that all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm may simultaneously attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi together with me.
Then, one invokes the Triple Gem, saying:
"With single-minded devotion, I invoke all the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Sanghas within the dust-mote lands throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm;
as well as the Vajrapāṇi, Guhyapada, and Dharma-protecting Devas and Kings."
Devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, brahmins, sages, and all the assembly of holy ones:
we pray that you will not violate your original vows,
but out of compassion for sentient beings, descend upon this site of practice as we, the assembly, invite you with harmonious incense and flowers.
Regarding the ritual for manifesting the seal [of the Buddha] upon the altar, according to the *Altar Construction Ritual* (*Jiantanyi*),
if there is no Buddha image on the altar,
one should form the seal of the Bodhisattva "Just Having Aroused the Resolve to Turn the Wheel of Dharma" (*Cai fayi zhuan falun pusa*).
Regarding the ritual for manifesting the seal of the maṇḍala,
the *Sāhasrabhuja-sahasranetra-caryā-vidhi* states:
"With both hands, form the vajra-fists."
The power of progress, generosity, and wisdom are interlinked.

Thereupon, the entire realm of empty space becomes a great maṇḍala.
Now, one should follow the specific tradition:
visualize the lords and retinues of the five families filling the realm of empty space, suddenly appearing with brilliant clarity.

the head seat (śrī-bhadra) holds the incense burner, kneels on his right knee, and addresses the Buddha.

homage to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the One Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, the Sugata, the Knower of the World.

Amitābha Buddha who conceals his body, and all other Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, who eternally abide in all worlds—
may these World-Honored Ones compassionately regard me.
Whatever heavy sins I have committed in this life or in previous lives,
since beginningless saṃsāra— whether committed by myself,
caused to be committed by others, witnessed being committed, or rejoiced in— [I now confess them all].
Whether it be property belonging to a stūpa, to the Saṃgha, or to the Saṃgha of the four quarters,
if one takes it oneself, causes another to take it, sees it being taken and rejoices in it,
these constitute the five ānantarya offenses.
Whether performed by oneself, caused to be performed by another, or seen being performed with approval—
regarding the ten unwholesome paths of action,
whether performed by oneself, caused to be performed by another, or seen being performed with approval.
Regarding the karmic obstructions created by their misdeeds— whether concealed or unconcealed—
they ought to fall into the various evil destinies of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals,
or into such places as the borderlands, the low-born, and the mlecchas.
I now repent of all the karmic obstructions created by my transgressions.
May the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
bear witness to me and keep me in their mindful recollection.
Furthermore, before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
I spoke these words:
"Whether in this life or in other lives..."
Whatever roots of goodness they have cultivated, such as practicing generosity or maintaining pure precepts—
even giving a single morsel of food to an animal—
or practicing pure conduct.
The roots of goodness for maturing all sentient beings;
the roots of goodness for practicing bodhi;
and the roots of goodness for unsurpassed wisdom.
Gathering all together, calculating and weighing them,
one dedicates them entirely toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
just as the Buddhas of the past, future, and present have performed their dedications.
I likewise dedicate in this way:
I repent of all transgressions; May all Buddhas rejoice, And through the merits of all Buddhas, May I attain supreme wisdom.
To the Buddhas of the past, future, and present, The most supreme among sentient beings,
oceans of immeasurable merit— I now take refuge and pay homage to all those Who are the lions among men throughout the worlds of the ten directions in the three periods of time.
With my body, speech, and mind purified, I prostrate to all, everywhere, without exception.
By the majestic power of Samantabhadra’s vows and conduct, I appear before all Tathāgatas;
From one body, I manifest bodies as numerous as atoms in a buddha-field, Prostrating to every Buddha throughout those atom-like fields.
Within a single atom are Buddhas as numerous as all atoms, each dwelling amidst assemblies of Bodhisattvas;
so it is with every atom throughout the inexhaustible Dharma-realm— deeply believing that all Buddhas completely fill them,
each producing from oceans of all voices an infinite array of wondrous words and phrases.
Throughout all kalpas of the future, I shall praise the Buddha’s ocean of profound virtues with the most excellent and wondrous flower garlands, with music, ointments, and parasols—
with such supreme articles of adornment as these, I shall make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
With the most excellent garments and the most excellent incense, with powdered incense, burning incense,
and lamps and candles— each as vast as Mount Sumeru— I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
With a mind of expansive and supreme resolve, I have deep faith in all the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Through the power of Samantabhadra’s vows and conduct, I universally make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Whatever evil karma I have created in the past, Arising from beginningless greed, hatred, and delusion,
And produced by my body, speech, and mind— All of this I now confess.
I rejoice in all the merits of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, of those in the two vehicles—
both those still training and those beyond training— and of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas.
I rejoice in all the lamps of the world throughout the ten directions, who first achieved the realization of Bodhi.
I now exhort you all to turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma;
If the Buddhas wish to manifest parinirvāṇa, I shall exhort them all with utmost sincerity:
"May you remain for as many eons as there are motes of dust in the lands, To bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings."
All merit from prostrations, praises, and offerings, The request for the Buddhas to remain in the world and turn the wheel of Dharma,
Rejoicing in and repenting of all roots of goodness— I dedicate these to sentient beings and the path of the Buddha.
By means of these supreme merits, I dedicate them to the unsurpassed, true Dharmadhātu.
The Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha in their essential nature and characteristics, The seal of samādhi that harmonizes the two truths—
I now dedicate all these oceans of immeasurable merit To all sentient beings who,
through body, speech, and mind, Have harbored views, slandered, or disparaged my Dharma and its like.
All such karmic obstructions are entirely extinguished without remainder;
In every thought-moment, wisdom pervades the entire dharma-realm.
He extensively delivers sentient beings without ever regressing, Until the exhaustion of empty space and the worlds, And until all sentient beings, karma, and afflictions are exhausted.
May these four dharmas, vast and boundless, likewise be dedicated;
thus I address all Buddhas of the ten directions,
as well as Prajñāpāramitā, the Bodhisattvas, Vajradevas, and others.
And all the immeasurable noble ones of the various paths of action— I, [Name],
now, by means of great compassion and riding upon the Buddha’s spiritual power,
invoke them from throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
Within the three realms of suffering, the hells, and all evil destinies;
throughout kalpas of desolation, all hungry ghosts;
and within the various offices of Yama, the celestial bureaus, and the earthly courts.
The karmic-path officials, Brahmins, and seers;
the spirits of those who died long ago in the wilderness;
the various devas of the void and their retinues; and the diverse classes of ghosts and spirits.
I pray that all Buddhas, Prajñāpāramitā, Bodhisattvas, Vajra Deities,
and other immeasurable sages and holy ones, as well as the various paths of karma,
will bestow their majestic light, increase their compassion, and grant their protective mindfulness.
I universally pray that throughout the ten directions and the entirety of the realm of empty space,
the celestial bureaus, the earthly courts, the officials of the karmic paths,
the innumerable hungry ghosts, and the parents from many past lives— may they all [attain liberation].
Brahmanical seers who have long since passed away;
all those bound by enmity over wealth and life;
and various classes of spirits and ghosts of diverse lineages, each with their respective retinues.
Riding upon the power of the Tathāgata, they will certainly descend at this time;
they shall receive the supreme and wondrous flavor of the Tathāgata’s Dharma,
and be fully satisfied by the pure, nectar-like food and drink.
Moisten the field of the body with merit and wisdom;
arouse the bodhicitta and forever leave behind deviant conduct;
take refuge in and revere the Triple Gem and practice great compassion.
Benefiting sentient beings while seeking the unsurpassed path,
they do not undergo the various evil fruits of suffering within saṃsāra;
they are always born into noble families and remain free from all fears.
"May my body be ever pure; may I realize the unsurpassed path"—thus he makes these three supplications.
The method for making offerings while directing the mind is explained in the second fascicle of the *Susiddhikara-sūtra-upāyika-vidhi*.
Regarding the offering of the mind:
one should imagine that all flowers of the water and land, not belonging to any owner,
fill the ten directions throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space.
And they presented to humans and devas clouds of exquisite unguents,
fragrant incense, lamps, banners, pennants, parasols, and canopies,
as well as various kinds of drums, music, song, dance, and vocal performances.
Pearl nets were suspended with various jeweled bells;
flower garlands, white whisks, and exquisite small bells and chimes [resounded];
and *kaṅkani* nets adorned the wish-fulfilling jewel trees.
Clouds of garments;
celestial foods of every kind, most excellent, fragrant, and delicious;
and various palatial towers adorned with precious pillars.
The practitioner visualizes clouds of celestial ornaments for adorning the body, such as crowns and necklaces,
filling the entirety of space with their mental focus.
To make offerings with such a sincere mind is the most supreme and wondrous way.

In performing any offering, one should possess this method;
furthermore, all offerings to the yoga [deities] rely upon mantras and mudrās,
as well as recitation for accomplishment and the movement of the mind.
Place the palms together at the crown of the head;
thus the method of perfecting the offering is complete. Having directed the mind, one says:
"I offer food to the Triple Gem; I shall present this food to the Triple Gem."
First, form the three-pointed mudrā:
place the dhyāna finger (the little finger) upon the head of the dāna finger (the index finger);
extend the śīla, kṣānti, and vīrya fingers (the middle, ring, and thumb fingers).
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajrayakṣa hūṃ. Recite this mantra twenty-one times.
Visualize great flames of fire issuing from the tips of the three fingers;
as the hands move like a fan over all the māras,
recite the *Ākāśavikaraṇa* mantra.
Oṃ svābhāvika-tathatā-svabhāva-tan-maya svābhāvika-tathatā-svabhāva-tan-maya svābhāvika-tathatā-svabhāva-tan-maya. Recite this three times.
Visualize that all food vessels are empty.
Within those empty spaces, visualize great precious vessels filled with nectar (*amṛta*).
Recite "Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ" twenty-one times to consecrate it as the wisdom nectar. Then, perform the *bali-mudrā* (offering-food seal).
Look upward with both hands;
place the two palms forward so that their sides touch,
and bring the tips of the two ring fingers together so that their sides meet.
Slightly bend the two index fingers so that their broad sides touch the sides of the middle fingers;
the two thumbs should likewise touch the sides of the index fingers.

One should universally offer and enjoy [these things], giving rise to a heart of joy;
whatever one seeks or prays for will certainly be granted permission.
Alternatively, one may extensively welcome the noble ones into the maṇḍala.
Having performed the detailed prostrations and praises, one then offers the food.
Having completed the various offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments,
one silently recites the verse for offering food.
I now offer this nectar-food, equal in measure to Mount Sumeru, surpassing in color, fragrance, and delicious flavor, pervading all of space.
May the Guru and the Triple Gem compassionately accept it.
Next, I offer to the protectors of the Exoteric and Esoteric teachings, and finally to all sentient beings throughout the realm of phenomena.
Enjoying full satisfaction, may joy arise; May all demonic obstacles be dispelled and peace bestowed.
On this day, may the patrons and their kin Have calamities eliminated and merit gathered, with longevity extended.
May all that is sought be accomplished as desired, And may there be auspiciousness at all times.
May the assembly recite this praise of the Three Jewels:
The World-Honored One, of great compassion and wondrous adornment, Perfectly endowed with clear understanding and all-encompassing wisdom,
Able to bestow blessings and insight like a vast ocean— To all such Tathāgatas, I pay homage and offer praise.
The essential nature of the self is inherently free from all desires; one who can practice accordingly is liberated from the evil realms.
This is the most profound and wondrous principle; I pay homage to the Sublime Dharma.
Within the path of liberation, it is the supreme liberation; those who uphold the pure precepts are worthy of veneration.
Born from an excellent field of merit in a supreme place, I pay homage to that Great Assembly.
Next, he enters the samādhi of Avalokiteśvara;
with the syllables *Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ*, he immediately enters the samādhi of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Close your eyes, clarify your mind,
and visualize yourself as perfectly white like the pure moon.
Upon this pure lunar disc at your heart, visualize the syllable *HŪṂ*, which radiates great light.
The syllable transforms into an eight-petaled lotus flower.
Upon the flower’s pedestal is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
his marks and signs clearly distinct.
The left hand holds a lotus flower,
and the right hand makes the gesture of opening petals.
This Bodhisattva then reflects as follows:
Within the bodies of all sentient beings,
each possesses this flower of awakening;
the pure dharma-realm is untainted by afflictions.
Upon each of the eight petals of the lotus,
a Tathāgata sits in meditative equipoise with legs crossed,
facing the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Adorned with a circular halo around the neck, his body is golden in color and radiates brilliant light.
Visualize this eight-petaled lotus flower gradually expanding and increasing in size until it is equal to space.
He then formed this thought:
"May these flowers of awakening, by their illuminating contact with the ocean-like assembly of Tathāgatas,
become a vast and magnificent offering."
If the mind does not shift from this meditative concentration,
one will give rise to profound compassion for infinite sentient beings;
those who are touched and illuminated by these flowers of awakening [will likewise be transformed].
One attains complete liberation from all sufferings and afflictions, becoming identical in appearance and marks to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Then, one visualizes the lotus flower gradually contracting until its size is equal to one's own body.
Then, having bound the seal of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, one empowers the four places—
the heart, forehead, throat, and crown—
such that at each location of the seal, the syllable *hrīḥ* is formed.
For this mudrā, interlace the two hands with the backs facing outward.
Join the two index fingers together like lotus petals,
and extend the two thumbs side by side, pointing upward.

Next, entering the Samādhi of Avalokiteśvara, he calmed his mind and closed his eyes to contemplate, within his heart, a full, bright, and pure moon disc.
Upon it was the seed-syllable *Āḥ*, which emitted light to form a lotus flower.
In the midst of the flowers is one Avalokiteśvara, Perfectly endowed with the marks and signs, beyond compare.
His left hand holds a wondrous lotus flower; His right hand makes the gesture of opening a petal.
The Bodhisattva contemplates the bodies of sentient beings, Each possessing a lotus flower of awakening.
The pure dharma-realm is free from delusion and defilement;
upon each of the eight petals sits a Tathāgata in the meditative posture of full lotus.
Each faces Avalokiteśvara, whose neck is adorned with a circular halo and whose body is golden in color, radiating a brilliant and most dazzling light.
Next, visualize that the flower gradually unfolds and expands, its magnitude pervading the entire realm of empty space.
Contemplate that this Awakened Flower illuminates the Dharma-realm; it is a vast offering to the ocean-like assembly of Tathāgatas.
If one’s mind does not waver from this samādhi, one will compassionately regard all sentient beings.
The awakened flower shines upon one, liberating them from suffering and affliction;
One then becomes equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, as the lotus gradually contracts until it is the same size as oneself.
Furthermore, forming the seal of the Sovereign Avalokiteśvara, empower the four locations while reciting the secret mantra; Thus, one’s own body also becomes equal to Avalokiteśvara.
Oṃ vajratāramā hṛīḥ. While forming this mudrā, recite the mantra.
By consecrating the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head,
one becomes identical to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
while entering into meditative absorption, one recites this praise.

hook the thumbs and wisdom fingers together,
and extend the index and middle fingers upward, joined side-by-side.
Visualize opening the hells;
recite three times and pull three times to open them.

flames stream forth from the mudrā.

upon the lunar disc of the heart—

however, this [hell] is singled out because it is intended to focus the mind.

all the gates to the hells within every realm of existence shall open wide of their own accord upon encountering this seal-mantra.

"Only when all sentient beings have been delivered shall I realize Bodhi;
until hell is emptied, I vow not to become a Buddha."
Great Sage, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha,
we pray that you will not violate your original vow, but out of compassion for sentient beings,
come now at this hour to this Dharma assembly; the assembly invites you with harmonious incense and flowers.
With single-minded devotion,
we invoke all the solitary spirits of the six realms within the dharma-realm,
and the assembly of *pūtana* ghosts presided over by King Yama.
The multitudes of beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who cling to grass and wood,
the chi-mei and wang-liang spirits, lingering souls and orphaned ghosts,
and all those including one's own and others' deceased ancestors and kinsmen.

they recite divine mantras as they follow the light and arrive before the practitioner.

Once they had been summoned, they all assembled like clouds;
with a mind of compassion, he praised and consoled them,
causing them to rejoice and become thirsting for the Dharma.
Welcome, O Sons of the Buddhas! Because you have previously formed sublime karmic connections, you now encounter this auspicious assembly. Do not give rise to anxiety or fear;
with single-minded longing for the Dharma, do not let this moment pass you by.
Having moistened one's body with the precepts, one is swiftly led away from the realms of suffering;
once arrived at the site of enlightenment, one circumambulates the Buddha three times,
prostrates oneself in worship, and completes the dedication of merit.
Having paid homage to the assembly of noble ones, he withdrew and sat to one side.
From the eastern gate of the altar, he proceeded to the southern gate, where the inhabitants of the hells resided;

If one lacks roots of goodness, one will not be born among the assembly of the noble ones.
Instead, wandering through saṃsāra according to one's karma, in every place of birth from lifetime to lifetime,
one must constantly cultivate roots of goodness, practicing them without interruption, toward the supreme Triple Gem.
May we be born in a central land and diligently cultivate the True Dharma;
may we be free from illness and long-lived, with all enjoyments fully provided,
and endowed with supreme marks and signs, eloquence, wisdom, and the like.
Possessing the seven merits, one obtains a male body; having taken refuge in the supreme Triple Gem,
one leaves home in youth with the aspiration to meet a noble and holy teacher,
thereby immediately attaining the three types of training and protection.
Maintaining right mindfulness and right concentration at all times,
may you serve the sublime and supreme guru with joy; may the Three Supreme Jewels and the most excellent spiritual friends,
who possess the seven types of noble wealth, be pleased.
Just as the sun and its light are never separated for even a moment,
so too may I be free from pride and doubt, possessing contentment.
May I abandon evil conditions, which are like poisonous spirits, and take refuge in the supreme Triple Gem.
At the supreme place of the Three Jewels, the foundation of merit and original vows,
may I always take refuge and offer worship.

Just as the great earth remains ever steadfast and unshakable, so too should one regard the objects of the six sense-fields—forms and other phenomena—as being like mirages and magical illusions; thus should one realize them.
In this way, one should never fail to give rise to the supreme Triple Gem.
May I remain unstained by attachment to the objects of the five sensual desires;
may I never forget the bodhicitta, the supreme Three Jewels,
and all the profound and subtle teachings of the Mahāyāna.
With diligence as if extinguishing a fire on one's head, one constantly practices and trains;
when realizing incomparable, ultimate bodhi,
one is able to rescue those in the six realms through the four means of attraction— the most supreme Triple Gem.
The Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara who can rescue [beings] from the five turbidities;
the King of the Earth (Kṣitigarbha) with his great vows during the final age;
and all the worthy sages and deities who protect the Dharma.
I bear witness to the blazing protection of the Lamp of Dharma, the supreme Triple Gem,
and all the guardian deities who protect the nation, the Dharma, and the stupas and temples;
through their majestic and powerful splendor, may this great boundary be established as a protective enclosure.
May the venomous classes of enemies, Māras, and non-Buddhists be utterly destroyed;
may the hearts of the venomous classes of nāgas, ghosts, and celestial bodies be struck with terror.
May the Three Most Supreme Jewels swiftly cause the three calamities and five turbidities to be eliminated.
The seven calamities and eight fears are all extinguished in a single thought.
The hundred grains are abundant and the myriad things flourish.
The seven treasures are sufficient and the five flavors are fully provided—the most supreme Triple Gem.
Receiving the fourfold offerings, they enjoy them without lack;
by cultivating the eight fields of merit, they obtain auspiciousness and peace.
Throughout the entire land, Buddhist affairs flourish and the Wheel of Dharma is turned.
May the merit and wisdom of sentient beings increase and be fully perfected.
Through the power of the dharmatā of the causal origination of our roots of virtue,
and through the power of the gathering and sustaining grace of the Guru, Yidam, and Dakini— the supreme Triple Gem.
By the majestic power of the true dharma and secret mantras of the Triple Gem, may whatever vows are made be swiftly fulfilled.
The Supreme Triple Gem is able to bestow back upon the person who has offered; this is the merit of returning what was returned.
All the various merits thus obtained are like magical illusions and resemble dreamscapes;
the three spheres are empty in essence, and in their emptiness, all are utterly serene— the most supreme Triple Gem.
May there be auspiciousness by day and auspiciousness by night; may the Guru grant his grace, and may there be constant auspiciousness throughout the six periods of the day and night.
May the Three Jewels grant their grace, and may there be auspiciousness at all times. May the Dharma protectors provide constant protection.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the Western Quarter and to the ocean-like assembly of great Bodhisattvas and holy multitudes.
We pray only that all the transgressions of those who exist within the Dharma-realm, both living and deceased, may be [purified].

The *Yogacaryābhūmi-saṃgraha-yamāntaka-bali-vidhi* is hereby completed.
The Text for the Ten Classes of Lonely Spirits Namo to the Buddhas, Dharmas, and Sanghas of the ten directions and three times throughout the entirety of space;
to the Gurus, Protectors, and Deities; and to the fierce Mother Vidyārājñī, the worldly and transcendent Dharma-protecting deities who respond to this occasion.
Your compassion is vast and your great vows are profound;
your power is immeasurable, and you know and see all things completely.
We pray that you act as our witness, looking upon us with pity and protecting us with your mindfulness.
In the subterranean prisons of the Dharma-realm,
there are the Lord Yama, the eighteen lords of hell, the thirty great kings, the thirty-three kings, and the thirty-six kings;
as well as the eighteen masters of hell, the Ox-head attendants, and the Horse-headed rākṣasas.
The Lord commands the Lord of the Poisonless Ghost Kings;
nine ranks and twenty-four offices assist the King;
minor officials, department heads, and leaders hold their staffs.
The Lord of Purity, the Lord of Water, the Lord of Iron, the Lord of Earth, and the Lord of Fire;
the good and evil youths, all the Gonggao functionaries and jailers;
the gelded horses bearing spears, and all the rākṣasas.
Furthermore, those who inspect upon the earth are Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, their princes, and their generals;
the Six Fasting Days, the Eight Kings, the Thirty-two Ministers of Patience,
the Four Great Kings of Patience, and the Great Deities of the Five Paths.
Furthermore, there are ten classes of solitary spirits (*preta*):
first, all those who protect the boundaries and guard the frontiers within the Dharma-realm,
who exerted their strength and dedicated their lives while maintaining the lines of battle in military arrays.
For the multitude of orphaned spirits— officials, generals, soldiers, and commoners— who have sacrificed their lives for the sake of the state;
and for all those in the second dharma-realm who carry debts of wealth,
owe their very lives, whose consciousnesses are bound by fetters, and who meet death during childbirth.
The spirits of those who have died as enemies or creditors, those who have suffered miscarriages, and the orphaned souls;
thirdly, all those in the realm of lightness and frivolity who have shown irreverence toward the Triple Gem and have been unfilial toward their parents.
The assembly of solitary spirits of the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and false views;
and all those in the fourth dharma-realm who have drowned in rivers and streams or perished at sea while trading.
The assembly of solitary souls who were swept away and drowned while seeking treasures amidst wind and waves;
the fifth dharma-realm: the assembly of solitary souls from all frontier regions and among the barbarians who died due to heterodox views;
the sixth dharma-realm: all those who abandoned their homelands and died as travelers in distant provinces.
The multitude of orphaned souls who wander aimlessly, without support or refuge; in the seventh dharma-realm,
all those who have gone to rivers, wells, blades, or ropes, or who have leaped into fire or off cliffs,
where walls collapse, houses fall, trees break, and crags shatter.
The multitudes of orphaned spirits who died untimely deaths from being bitten by beasts or injured by insects;
those whose lives ended within the various realms of the eighth dharma-world;
and those who did not abide by the laws of the king.
The multitudes of orphaned spirits of those who were robbed by bandits and thieves, those who harbored grievances and swallowed their injustices,
those executed by the great blade or dismembered, and those who violated the law.
The ninth dharma-realm consists of all male and female slaves and attendants who diligently exert their strength and entrust their lives to the multitude of impoverished,
lowly, and orphaned spirits.
The tenth [assembly] consists of all those in the realm who are blind, deaf, mute, lame, or have withered hands;
those afflicted by chronic illnesses, abscesses, and debilitating injuries;
and the widowers, widows, orphans, the solitary, and the multitude of orphaned spirits without protection.
Furthermore, according to the Dharma, the realm of the King of Ghosts governs the *pretas*—the *vairambhas*—who are as numerous as the sands of hundreds of billions of Ganges Rivers.
Among these, there are those whose names I have seen or heard and those whose names I have not; they comprise countless species and clans within the human world.
Residing among the grasses and trees adjacent to the city walls,
they harbor the consciousnesses of vengeful spirits and the numinous essences of all things—
those who have committed suicide, those who have perished, or those whose bodies died in the ranks of battle.
To those who have no support or refuge, whose remains are cast aside and their bones exposed;
to those whose souls are famished for lack of offerings, and to the multitudes of *chimei* and *wangliang*, as well as the lingering spirits and ethereal echoes: [I offer this].
Furthermore, there are ghosts of great power, yakṣas, māras, and ghosts that afflict humans;
ghosts of internal obstruction, ghosts of external obstruction, and unimpeded ghosts.
There are also nine classes, ten classes, and thirty-six classes of ghostly hosts.
May the power of the Triple Gem— the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—
the power of the dependent origination of the Dharmadhātu,
and the power of the Great Compassionate Avalokiteśvara.
The power of the profound vow of Kṣitigarbha;
the power of the merit as I now perceive it;
and the power of empowerment through secret mantras and mudrās.
By the power of reciting the names of the Seven Tathāgatas and the power of the roots of goodness from this Dharma assembly for reciting the sutras,
we now summon all those of the various classes of solitary souls and hungry ghosts within the Dharma-realm.
All their retinues gathered like clouds.
These foods and drinks were transformed so as to fill the entire dharma-realm throughout the void.
From all the mountains, plains, and great earth, pools of clear and cool water welled up.
All green ponds and rivers are transformed into vast oceans of milk;
the twelve classes of sentient beings are fully satiated with the food of the Dharma,
and the twenty-five realms of existence are provided with the perfect abundance of all instruments of joy.
The three karmas become lucid and the six sense faculties are purified;
body and mind are light, tranquil, cool, and blissful.
Merit and wisdom increase in brilliance, and all sought-after aspirations are fulfilled.
Take refuge in the Triple Gem and resolve to attain Bodhicitta.
By cultivating the practices of a Bodhisattva, you shall achieve the Way of Buddhahood; may the assembly harmonize with this vow so that it may be fulfilled.
For the path to the hidden realm is vast and remote.
The waves of the ocean of suffering are deep;
were it not for the power of secret mantras,
how could the souls submerged therein be delivered?
For this reason, a special Dharma assembly was established;
the monastic community was reverently gathered,
and they chanted and expounded the secret mantras.
By consecrating this sublime Dharma-food with such merit,
may it be universally bestowed upon the infinite.
I humbly pray that the boiling cauldrons may transform into lotus ponds of the eight virtues,
and the blazing furnace coals [may likewise change].
The fragrant canopies weighing six *zhū* are formed;
the dense sword-trees become the *nāgapuṣpa* flowers for the three assemblies.
The towering mountain of blades became the Vulture Peak of the Five Indias;
the molten copper and copper pillars [were likewise transformed].
They transform the Dharma-banner of nectar;
they grind iron balls with iron to create a mani-jewel throne.
The Ox-Head Hell-Warden,
by upholding the three virtues, realizes the three bodies;
even creditors and enemies [can become aids].
Having resolved the ten fetters and abandoned the ten evils,
they will frequently be born as parents;
from this point on, they shall enter the state of sainthood and transcend the mundane world.
All sentient beings shall,
from this point forward, obtain peace and happiness,
and cultivate the path of friendship.
Rejoicing in the practice of giving,
one awakens to the Amitābha of one's own fundamental nature and realizes that the Pure Land is but the manifestation of one's own mind.
Universally equal to the Dharma-realm and extending to all sentient beings,
may all together bathe in these auspicious conditions.
Thus one shall together perfect the Way of the Buddha.

Praise of the Three Refuges: With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Buddha, the Honored One Among the Two-Legged, whose three types of awakening are perfected and who is endowed with myriad virtues.
The Teacher who tames gods and humans, Aḥ Hūṃ, the Great Compassionate Father of both ordinary and holy beings,
manifests from the realm of reality to respond to conditions through compassionate transformation.
Pervasively erect throughout the three periods of time and horizontally encompassing the ten directions, he thunders the Dharma-thunder and beats the Dharma-drum.
Widely expounding the provisional and ultimate teachings, with the syllables *Aḥ* and *Hūṃ*, he opens wide the path of skillful means; if one takes refuge, the sufferings of hell can be extinguished.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the Honored One, Dharmayā, who has transcended desire.
His precious treasury contains jade caskets and silk scrolls;
they were compiled in the Western Regions and translated into the Eastern Land with the syllables *AṂ HŪṂ*.
The Patriarch propagated the discernment of the wise, composing commentaries on the scriptures;
he distinguished the three vehicles into sudden and gradual, and established the essential tenets of the five teachings.
Ghosts and spirits revered him, and dragons and devas protected him.
Guiding the deluded like a finger pointing at the moon, Aḥ Hūṃ—the true nectar that dispels heat.
If one takes refuge, the sufferings of the hungry ghosts can be extinguished.
With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to the Saṅgha, the most honored among the assembly.
With the five virtues as one's teacher and the six harmonies as one's companions,
taking the welfare of sentient beings as one’s vocation and the propagation of the Dharma as one’s domestic duty,
one should avoid the clamor of the dust of the world and always remain seated in meditation in a place of stillness.
He covered his body with garments of coarse wool and filled his belly by gathering fresh wild greens;
his almsbowl subdued dragons, and his mendicant’s staff tamed tigers.
The lamp of Dharma shines eternally and universally; Aḥ Hūṃ. This seal of the lineage has been transmitted and entrusted.
By taking refuge, one can extinguish the suffering of the animal realm.
